title: Is two greater than negative three, and why?
description: Two pairs of numbers are compared by their places on the number line. The number further to the right is the greater one, and the movement between them confirms it.
teaching_notes: One idea: on the number line, the number further to the right is the greater one. Watch for students who think negative three is greater because three is bigger than two.

video_script.why: The child sees that greater and less are read from the places on the number line, and that the digit alone does not decide a negative number.
video_script.substitution: The book's own number line from negative ten to ten, with each pair of numbers placed on it.
video_script.anchor: the number line of the book from negative ten to ten
video_script.payoff_line: The number further right on the number line is greater.

final_answer.value: Yes, 2 > -3 because 2 is to the right of -3. Yes, -2 < 3 because 3 is to the right of -2
final_answer.spoken: yes, two is greater than negative three, because two is to the right of negative three; and yes, negative two is less than three, because three is to the right of negative two

maths_rules: smaller numbers lie to the left of bigger numbers
-3 is 3 steps left of 0 and 2 is 2 steps right of 0, so 2 is to the right of -3: 2 > -3
-2 is 2 steps left of 0 and 3 is 3 steps right of 0, so 3 is to the right of -2: -2 < 3
check: 2 - (-3) = 5, a forward movement of 5 from -3 to 2; 3 - (-2) = 5, a forward movement from -2 to 3
slip: 3 is bigger than 2 as a count, but -3 is on the left side, so -3 < 2
